program.section_heading: Business Administration: General Business Concentration - Associate of Science Degree and Certificate of Achievement - MAS524/C/MCE524
outcomes: Use technology to analyze business decisions and to enhance business communications.
Apply basic business and accounting calculations and analyses.
Have an understanding of legal practices relating to business.
Explain the managerial applications of accounting reports and ratios to the business enterprise.
Analyze the law as it pertains to business organizations and determine the legal management of the various forms of law.
Analyze the business elements that comprise the logistics function.
Develop and apply principles of moral judgment and ethical behavior to business situations.
Anticipate and pose problems relative to understanding and supervising personnel.
Identify and analyze human relations techniques appropriate to a managerial role.
Explain and develop the marketing mix, including an analysis of the marketing mix variables—product, place, price, and promotion.

notes: The catalog section covers both the A.S. Degree and the Certificate of Achievement with one shared set of requirements and one Program Learning Outcomes list; both were recorded for the A.S. Degree.
The heading is printed three times; the third version lists codes MAS524/MAS524B/MAS524C/MCE524. The first version was used as section_heading.
Catalog prints codes with hyphens (e.g., ACC-1A, BUS-47, BUS-200); these were matched to closed-list entries ACC 1A, BUS47, BUS200, etc., and are not treated as catalog additions.
Within the electives, 'Select one: BUS-47 OR MAG-47' (3.00 units) is recorded as one entry with MAG-47 as its alternative.
BUS-200 is printed as 1.00-4.00 variable units.
No GE pattern is named; the degree text refers only generally to general education and graduation requirements in the college catalog.
Several core courses are marked '( Historical )' in the catalog (ACC-1A, BUS-10, BUS-18A, ACC-1B, BUS-18B); a reviewer may want to confirm their status for 2026-2027.
